title: fix(runtime)!: a multi-package artifact binds each package body's hooks and functions under that body's package, as its actions (ADR-0150 D3/D4)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg4qDVGszsiYzjhEdhEHRXro)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaP1iy4RSEQbW6177G

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：多包制品（`packages[]`）启动时，每个包体的 hooks 和 functions 登记在该包自己名下（`app:<包 id>`），不再全部压在制品自己的 id 下；规则与 #32333 对动作的处理同一套。没有唯一归属的函数（两包共用、两包同声明、或制品名下的 hook 点名了别的包体的函数）仍留在制品 id 下，连同点名它的 hook，与改前一致。
- 为什么改：改前包 B 的流程调 B 自己的函数会被拒（`outside-closure`），包 B 的 hook 找不到 B 自己登记的函数，违反 ADR-0150 D3/D4「按引用方所在包解析」。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（BREAKING，第一方计数 0），共四处：① 非制品自身的包 B 的 hook 点名 B 没声明、别的包体声明的函数，改后绑定时以 `INVALID_REFERENCE` 拒绝；② 制品自身包的流程点名只有别的包体声明的函数，改后只经声明的依赖闭包可达，否则 `outside-closure`；③ 顶层无 manifest 的输入与某个包体同名 hook，两条都不绑定并记 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`；④ 顶层函数只被某一个包体 B 的 hook 点名时归 `app:B`，制品自身包按 id 读或卸载不再含它，制品自身包的流程点名它须经依赖闭包。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` 的 `hookBindingGroups`（hook 按名字、函数按声明包分组，一遍决定哪些函数留在制品 id 下）与 `bindAppArtifactHandlers` 的拆除段（记录的每个 owner 都拆；被丢弃包体的函数离场；重绑把函数换给别的 owner 时从旧 owner 撤下）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app-artifact-handlers.test.ts`，预期 27 个用例全绿；`[ADR-0150 D4] a multi-package artifact binds each body's hooks and functions` 下 14 个是本卡新增。
- 需要你做的：本 PR 是 BREAKING（`!` 标题，收窄），落地前需要你一句话；契约复审与 epic 红线复读由席位去请。

Fixes #32349

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — a hook in package body B, a body other than the artifact's own, whose `handler` names a function B does not declare and another body A of the same artifact does is no longer bound: FROM bound and running A's function (every hook and function of the artifact was registered under the artifact's own id) TO refused at bind with `INVALID_REFERENCE` (400), logged at error, the hook never running; and a flow of the artifact's own package whose `script` node names a function only another body declares, which no hook under the artifact's id names, FROM running it as the artifact's own TO the package-scoped answer (ADR-0150 D3): that body's function when its package is in the flow package's declared closure, else refused `outside-closure`. And a hook name one package body other than the artifact's own declares, which the artifact's top level also carries for an input with no `manifest` (the ADR-0130 residual), FROM both hooks bound under the artifact's id TO neither bound, refused at bind and logged at error with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`ambiguous-in-environment`) naming the body: nothing in the artifact tells the residual's copy from the body's, the shape #32355 refused for a job; a residual twin of the artifact's own body's hook binds as before. And a function the artifact's top level declares (an input with no `manifest`, or the ref `os build` lowers out of a body's hook) that the hooks of exactly one body B other than the artifact's own name, and no hook under the artifact's id names, FROM registered under the artifact's id TO registered under B's package: `functionHoldersOf(name).packageItem(ARTIFACT_ID)` FROM the entry TO `undefined` and `packageItem(B)` FROM `undefined` TO the entry, `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:ARTIFACT_ID')` FROM removing it TO leaving it, and a flow of the artifact's own package whose `script` node names it FROM resolved as its own TO B's function through its declared closure, else refused `outside-closure`. Three engine calls move with it: `unregisterHooksByPackage('app:ARTIFACT_ID')` and `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:ARTIFACT_ID')` FROM removing every body's hooks and functions TO removing only what stays bound under the artifact's id (its own body's, the top level's hooks, the top level's functions no single other body's hooks alone name, and what the function rules below keep there), and `functionHoldersOf(name).packageItem(ARTIFACT_ID)` FROM answering every body's function TO answering only those. Measured first-party: 0 (the one first-party composition, `examples/app-multi-package`, declares no hook, function or flow; no first-party code calls those engine methods with a composed artifact's id outside the binder). It also widens: a hook in body B naming a function the engine holds under B's own package (`app:B`) binds, where it was refused `INVALID_REFERENCE`; and a flow in body B naming B's own function, or a top-level function only B's hooks name, runs it, where it was refused `outside-closure` (or ran the artifact's owner's holder) whenever B's closure did not reach the artifact's own package, unless a hook under the artifact's id names that function too, which keeps it there as before.
Metadata-protocol: semantic — the name an author writes in a package body's hook `handler`, or in a flow `script` node's function, now reaches that body's own function (ADR-0150 D3), where it reached any body's; no key, value or schema changes. This corrects the claim's `Clause-②: no`, which the narrowing rows below disprove; the claim's `semantic` holds.
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/` and no page under `content/docs/` teaches a multi-package artifact's hooks or functions, or a hook naming another package's function (`content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx` "A project is a multi-package artifact" names `manifest: 'preserve'` and says nothing about hooks or functions; grep of both trees for `composeStacks`, `packages[]` and multi-package hook/function wording found no sentence this PR makes false).

## What changes

`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` (plus its test and the changeset), and one sentence of #32333's pending changeset `.changeset/32245-compose-object-less-action-per-namespace.md` ("Hooks and functions stay under the artifact's owner." → "Hooks and functions bind per package body by the same rule since #32349."), which this PR made false; nothing else in that file. `packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts` is unchanged: its `ownPackageFunction` already reads the owner a hook is bound under, so it reads the body's own once the binder binds per body.

- **`hookBindingGroups(bundle, owner)`**, beside #32333's `actionBindingGroups` and sharing its body walk (`artifactBodies`, in `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`'s order). A bundle with no `packages[]` is one group under the artifact's owner, exactly as before. Otherwise it binds what the reconciled artifact carries (`collectBundleHooks(bundle)`, `collectBundleFunctionEntries(bundle)`) and reads each body for who declares what:
  - **Hooks, by name** (card Do 2, "one owner unless held apart"): one body carries the name ⇒ under that body's `app:PACKAGE_ID`; no body ⇒ (the residual) under the artifact's owner; two or more bodies ⇒ under the artifact's owner, unless held apart under child N's namespace co-owner rule (`namespaceNameConflicts` from `@objectstack/objectql`, the rule the install gate applies to a hook name), and then each body binds its own hooks of the name under its own package. **Residual twin:** a name that would go to a body other than the artifact's own, and that the top level carries beside the bodies (counted, never compared, as `jobDeclaringPackages` counts a job's for #32355), binds no hook at all and is logged at error naming the body.
  - **Functions, by declaring body**: one body declares it ⇒ that body's package; none (a top-level function, or a ref `os build` lowered out of a body's hook) ⇒ the owner of the hooks that name it, else the artifact's owner. **One pass then decides what stays under the artifact's owner** (a function keeps one package holder, and a hook resolves its `handler` in its own group's package only), each with the hooks that go with it, as on `main`: a function no body declares that two or more owners' hooks name (every hook naming it); a function two or more bodies declare, a hand-written artifact only (the declaring bodies' hooks); and a function one body other than the artifact's own declares that a hook under the artifact's owner names (the declaring body's hooks; epic E1). Any other body's hook naming a function only other bodies declare is refused (row 6). The pass reads the bundle's own function names (`Object.keys`), never `name in` the map (review N3).
- **`bindAppArtifactHandlers`**: one `ql.bindHooks(...)` per group, each under `packageId: group.owner` with that group's functions, each in its own try/catch. The withheld-hook rule (`withholdHooksWithoutBody`) applies across every group; the unrecognized-effect warning is said once per name; the counts sum over groups.
- **Teardown** (card Do 3): every owner the artifact's previous bind on this engine recorded, plus every owner the new bind names, has its actions and hooks removed; a recorded owner the new bind no longer names (a dropped body) also has its functions unregistered. Owners still named keep their functions, replaced by name, as before, **except a function the new bind gives to another owner**, which leaves the owner the previous bind gave it (`releaseMovedFunctions`: the engine removes by package only, so the functions that owner keeps, the ones the previous bind gave it and the ones its hooks now name, are read first and registered again, with each name's bare slot put back). The record (`boundOwnersByEngine`) now holds the owners and the functions given to each.
- Kept as they were: the job rulings Q1-B (`pull`) and Q2-O1 (`organization`), the ⛔ line on platform-internal scheduled work, and the ⛔ line that nothing resolves a bare name to a package.

## FROM → TO (every moved answer)

Measured on `origin/main` (FROM; the base binder restored over the head's tests, or the ablation that puts every hook and function back under the artifact's owner) and this head (TO). A = the artifact's own package (its id, the last input's manifest under `preserve`); B, C = other package bodies.

| # | Answer | FROM | TO | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner B's declared function is registered under | `app:A` | `app:B` | pins (a), (c) |
| 2 | Owner B's hook is bound under (name only B carries) | `app:A` | `app:B` | pins (b), (c) |
| 3 | B's flow `script` naming B's function, B not depending on A | refused `outside-closure`, candidates `[A]` | resolved, `app:B`, runs B's | pin (a) |
| 4 | B's hook naming a function the engine holds under `app:B` | refused `INVALID_REFERENCE` | bound, fires | pin (b) |
| 5 | A hook name both bodies carry, two namespaces, each with its own function | both under `app:A`; `packageItem(B)` undefined | each under its own package, each fires its own | pin (c) |
| 6 | **Narrowing.** B's hook (B not the artifact's own) naming a function B does not declare and another body does | bound, runs that function | refused `INVALID_REFERENCE` at bind, logged at error, does not fire | pin (d) |
| 7 | **Narrowing.** A's flow `script` naming a function only B declares (no hook under `app:A` names it) | resolved `app:A` | A depends on B ⇒ resolved `app:B`; else refused `outside-closure` | pin (h), both arms |
| 8 | Re-bind that drops body B | B's hooks stop; B's functions stay registered (`packageHolders` = `[A]`) | B's hooks stop and its functions leave the engine (`[]`) | pin (e) |
| 9 | `unregisterHooksByPackage` / `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:A')`, `functionHoldersOf(n).packageItem(A)` | every body's | only what stays under `app:A`: A's own body's, the top level's hooks, the top level's functions no single other body's hooks alone name (row 15), and what rows 10, 16 and 18 keep there | follows from 1, 2, 15 |
| 10 | Function no body declares, named by the hooks of two owners | under `app:A` with both hooks | unchanged; one package holder, `sealBareNameHolders()` = `[]` | pin (f) |
| 11 | Residual hook (no body declares it) and the top-level function it names | under `app:A` | unchanged | CONTROL pin, second half |
| 12 | Bundle with no `packages[]` | one owner | unchanged | the file's other 13 tests |
| 13 | **Narrowing.** Hook name body B declares and the residual (an input with no manifest) declares too | both bound under `app:A`, both fire | neither bound; one error `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `packages: [B]`; the residual's function not attributed to B | pin (g) |
| 14 | Hook name the artifact's own body A declares and the residual declares too | both under `app:A` | unchanged | pin (g), second half |
| 15 | **Narrowing.** Top-level function (residual-declared, or a ref `os build` lowered out of B's hook) that only body B's hooks name | under `app:A`: `packageItem(A)` the entry, `packageItem(B)` undefined; `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:A')` removes it; A's flow resolves it as its own | under `app:B`: `packageItem(A)` undefined, `packageItem(B)` the entry; `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:A')` leaves it; A's flow resolves it through A's closure, else `outside-closure`; B's hook binds and runs it; B's flow resolves it as its own (widening) | pin (j); CONTROL pin, first half (review M1 a) |
| 16 | Top-level hook naming a function only body B declares (epic E1-a, review M1 b) | bound under `app:A`, runs B's function | unchanged: the function and B's own hooks naming it stay under `app:A`, all bind and run | pin (E1-a); ablated: `INVALID_REFERENCE` |
| 17 | Hook name two bodies of one judged namespace carry, one naming a function only B declares (epic E1-b) | the boot refuses the artifact before any bind; the binder alone binds under `app:A` | unchanged on both. The co-owner install refuses the second body: `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` → `refuseNamespaceNameConflicts` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:9403`, throwing at `:9797-9798`, `NamespaceNameConflictError`, `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` 422), inside `restoringOnRefusal` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1027`) at `AppPlugin.init`'s registration (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:660`), ahead of the bind in `start` (`:1863`) | pin (E1-b), both halves; ablated: `INVALID_REFERENCE` |
| 18 | Function two bodies declare (hand-written only: `composeStacks` refuses the pair with `STACK_COMPOSE_FUNCTION_CONFLICT`) (review N1) | under `app:A` with every hook | unchanged for the declaring bodies' hooks (under `app:A`, bound); another body's hook naming it is row 6 | pin (k) |
| 19 | Re-bind that gives a function to another owner while the old owner stays named (review S1) | unreachable (one owner) | it leaves the old owner (`packageHolders` = `[A]`), which keeps its other functions | pin (l); ablated: `['…beta', '…alpha']` |
| 20 | Hook firing order within one `priority` on one object and event (review S2, epic N2) | the reconciled order, one owner | grouped by owner, owners in the order their first hook appears; a hook a function rule keeps under `app:A` fires after A's other hooks of its priority. The engine's sort is stable, so ties follow registration order | changeset "Firing order"; not pinned |

## First-party census

- **Shipped multi-package artifacts:** one, `examples/app-multi-package` (core + orders, owner core). It declares no hook, no function and no flow (`git grep -nE "hooks|functions|flows" -- examples/app-multi-package` → 0 hits). Moved answers on it: **0**, rows 6, 7, 13 and 15 included.
- `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` callers outside tests: that example, and CLI/core plumbing that reads the shape (`packages/cli/src/commands/{compile,lint,migrate/meta}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/*`, `packages/core/src/stack-collections.ts`); none binds hooks or functions.
- Fixtures with `packages[]`: `packages/objectql/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-4.0.1-published-pages.artifact.json` (2 bodies, 0 hooks, 0 functions, 0 flows); `packages/cli/test/fixtures/option-b-collection-zoo.ts` (a CLI lowering fixture, never bound by the runtime).
- No first-party code calls `unregisterHooksByPackage`, `unregisterFunctionsByPackage` or `functionHoldersOf(…).packageItem` with a composed artifact's id outside the binder, and none calls the exported binder twice on one engine with callables (row 19's reach).

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.test.ts`, describe `[ADR-0150 D4] a multi-package artifact binds each body's hooks and functions under that body` (14 cases; ALPHA = `com.qa.bodies.alpha` is the artifact's id, BETA = `com.qa.bodies.beta`; each body installed as the boot installs it, so a caller's closure is the save door's):

- (a) a body-B flow runs B's own function (card pin 1)
- (b) a body-B hook binds B's own engine-registered function (card pin 2)
- (c) each body's hook of one name binds its own body's bundle function, both under their own packages
- (d) NARROWING: a body-B hook naming a function only body A declares is refused at bind
- (e) a body the new bundle drops stops running: its hooks stop firing and its functions leave the engine (card pin 3)
- (f) a function no body declares that two bodies' hooks name stays under the artifact's id with those hooks
- (g) NARROWING: a hook name body B declares and an input with no manifest declares too binds neither; when the body is the artifact's own, both bind as before
- (E1-a) a top-level hook naming a function only body B declares binds and runs it, the function and B's own hook of it under the artifact's id, as before
- (E1-b) a hook name two bodies of one namespace carry, naming a function only body B declares, binds as before; the install gate refuses the pair first
- (h) NARROWING: a flow of the artifact's own package naming a function only body B declares resolves it through its declared closure, else is refused `outside-closure` (row 7, both arms; review S3)
- (j) NARROWING: a top-level function only body B's hooks name is registered under B (row 15; review M1 a)
- (k) a function two bodies declare (a hand-written artifact) stays under the artifact's id with the declaring bodies' hooks (row 18; review N1)
- (l) a re-bind that moves a function to another owner takes it off the old owner, which keeps its other functions (row 19; review S1)
- CONTROL: a built artifact's body hook binds the ref its runtime module serves at the top level; a residual hook binds under the artifact's id

**Red first.** Round 1: the base binder restored over the new tests failed (a)–(e) and (g) with the FROM answers in the table. Round 2's new pins are measured red by the ablation that restores the base binding (every hook and function under the artifact's owner): (h) `{"status":"resolved","item":{"packageId":"app:com.qa.bodies.alpha",…}}` where `refused` was expected, (j) `expected [ 'com.qa.bodies.alpha' ] to deeply equal [ 'com.qa.bodies.beta' ]`, (l) its precondition the same; (E1-a), (E1-b) and (k) are green there by design (they keep `main`'s outcome) and red when their own rule is ablated, below.

**Green:** `Tests  27 passed (27)`.

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed binder, each restored to blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty):

| Rule ablated | Anchor → replacement | Red |
|---|---|---|
| per-body binding (all of it) | `if (!bodies) return …` → `if (!bodies \|\| owner) return …` | 9: (a)–(e), (g), (h), (j), (l) |
| E1 (owner-named function stays) | `if (from === owner \|\| !naming.has(owner)) continue;` → `… \|\| 'ABLATED_E1') continue;` | 2: (E1-a) `[ [ 'qa_res_borrow', … ] ]`, (E1-b) `[ [ 'qa_same', 'INVALID_REFERENCE' ] ]` |
| shared undeclared function (f) | `if (naming.size < 2) continue;` → `… \|\| 'ABLATED_F') continue;` | 2: (f), (l) |
| two-body function (N1) | `moveToOwner(name, declaring.map(ownerOf));` → `void 'ABLATED_N1';` | 1: (k) `[ [ 'qa_beta_twice', … ] ]` |
| re-bind move (S1) | `if (moved.length > 0) releaseMovedFunctions(` → `if (moved.length > 0 && !'ABLATED_S1') …` | 1: (l) `expected [ 'com.qa.bodies.beta', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ 'com.qa.bodies.alpha' ]` |
| top-level function to its one naming body (M1 a) | `: [...(namedBy.get(name) ?? [owner])];` → `: [owner];` | 3: (j), (l), CONTROL |

## DELIBERATE CORRECTION (`check-empty-changeset` red by design)

This PR rewrites one sentence of a pending release note it made false. It is not a changeset-name collision, and the note must not be restored from the base:

- `.changeset/32245-compose-object-less-action-per-namespace.md` (#32333's note), one sentence only, cleared by the seat in round 2:
  - before: "Hooks and functions stay under the artifact's owner."
  - after: "Hooks and functions bind per package body by the same rule since #32349."

The diff also changes code, so the confirming record is the seat's same-head at-tier contract-review PASS, which judges this sentence (pm-dispatch `references/landing-operations.md`). No maintainer wait is owed for it.

## Acceptance notes

- `hook-binder.ts` needed no change, so the card's file surface beyond `app-artifact-handlers.ts` is untouched. The one line outside it is the #32333 changeset sentence the seat cleared.
- Row 19's fix is the engine's: a function leaves the old owner's registration. The registry's bare-name claim the old owner recorded (`claimBareNameFunctions`) stays until `uninstallPackage`, as it does for a dropped body's functions: the registry has no public release for one claim, and `registry.ts` is outside this card. It is reachable only when the exported binder is called twice on one engine with callables (not the JSON install-local door).
- A function code outside this binder registered under a body's owner, which neither the previous bind gave that owner nor any of its hooks names, leaves with a row-19 release, as it does with a dropped body (review N6).
- The residual-twin rule (row 13) was added after the PR opened: measuring a composition with a manifest-less input showed the first head attributing the residual's hook, and its function, to the body that shares the name. Actions cannot reach this shape: `composeStacks` refuses a cross-stack action key with `STACK_COMPOSE_ACTION_KEY_COLLISION`, the residual included.
